(sec-module-systemutilities)=
# Module: systemUtilities

The functions of a whole system (#2997): quantities of the system from the contributions of its items -
SystemQuantity with SystemEnergy and SystemConstraintDrift, their sensors -, the residuals of the
constraints, the numerical Jacobian of a computation of the current state, and the system graph.
'from exudyn.utilities import *' includes this module.

- **Author**: Johannes Gerstmayr
- **Date**: 2026-10-16 (created; the functions came from advancedUtilities, solver and mainSystemExtensions)

(sec-systemutilities-loadpotentialenergy)=
## Function: LoadPotentialEnergy

[`LoadPotentialEnergy(mbs, loadNumber, configuration = exudyn.ConfigurationType.Current)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/systemUtilities.py#L174)

- **function description**: the potential energy of a constant load, zero in the reference configuration: $-\fv\tp \uv$ of the displacement $\uv$ of its marker point; None if the load has none that can be computed
- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem of the load
  - `loadNumber`: the load, a LoadIndex
  - `configuration`: the configuration its marker is evaluated in
- **output**: the potential energy as a float, or None for a load whose potential is not available: a load with a user function (it may depend on time), a body-fixed load, a torque (not conservative in 3D), a mass-proportional load on a body other than a mass point, a 1D mass or a rigid body
- **notes**: Covered are ForceVector and Coordinate loads on any marker that gives a position or a coordinate, and MassProportional loads on the bodies named above.


(sec-systemutilities-computeconstraintresiduals)=
## Function: ComputeConstraintResiduals

[`ComputeConstraintResiduals(mbs, velocityLevel = False, autoAssemble = True) -> list`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/systemUtilities.py#L361)

- **function description**: the residuals of all algebraic equations of the system in the current state - the drift of the constraints (#565); computed per item with mbs.ComputeItem, without a solver, so that it can be called at any time, e.g., in a PreStepUserFunction or a SensorUserFunction during a simulation
- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem
  - `velocityLevel`: False: the position-level constraints, ComputeItemType.ConstraintDrift - zero for the equations of velocity-level constraints (rolling disc, CoordinateConstraint with velocityLevel=True), which do not drift;
  - `True`: the equations at velocity level, ComputeItemType.AlgebraicEquations_t
  - `autoAssemble`: if True and mbs.systemIsConsistent=False, mbs.Assemble() is called first
- **output**: (type: list) [residuals, items], residuals is a numpy array with one entry per algebraic equation of the system (the numbering of the Lagrange multipliers, mbs.systemData.GetAECoordinates()), items the ObjectIndex or NodeIndex of each entry

*example*:

```python
  [residuals, items] = mbs.ComputeConstraintResiduals()
  k = np.argmax(abs(residuals))
  print('largest drift', residuals[k], 'in', items[k])
```


- **NOTE**: this function is directly available in MainSystem (mbs); it should be directly called as mbs.ComputeConstraintResiduals(...). For description of the interface, see the MainSystem Python extensions, {ref}`sec-mainsystemextensions-computeconstraintresiduals`


(sec-systemutilities-numericaljacobian)=
## Function: NumericalJacobian

[`NumericalJacobian(mbs, function, systemCoordinates, velocityLevel = False, epsilon = 1e-8)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/systemUtilities.py#L415)

- **function description**: the derivative of a computation of the current state of the system - an output variable, mbs.ComputeItem, a user function - by some of the system ODE2 coordinates or their velocities, by central differences; for tests of the Jacobians of an item, in particular of a user item, against mbs.ComputeItem
- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem, assembled
  - `function`: a function without arguments that computes the values from the current state, e.g.
  - `lambda`: mbs.ComputeItem(oBody, exu.ComputeItemType.ODE2LHS)
  - `systemCoordinates`: the indices of the system ODE2 coordinates to differentiate by, e.g. the coordinates of an object, mbs.systemData.GetObjectLTGODE2(objectNumber), or of a node, mbs.systemData.GetNodeLTGODE2(nodeNumber)
  - `velocityLevel`: False: by the coordinates; True: by their time derivatives
  - `epsilon`: the step of the central differences, absolute; 1e-8 as in the numerical differentiation of the solvers; the round-off error is about 1e-16/epsilon, the truncation error about epsilon**2 - 1e-6 is more accurate for smooth functions of coordinates of order 1
- **output**: the derivative as numpy array, (number of values of function) x (number of systemCoordinates); the state of the system is restored afterwards

*example*:

```python
  coordinates = mbs.systemData.GetObjectLTGODE2(oBody)
  numerical = NumericalJacobian(mbs, lambda: mbs.GetObjectOutputBody(oBody, exu.OutputVariableType.Velocity,
                                localPosition=[0.1,0,0]), coordinates, velocityLevel=True)
  analytic = mbs.ComputeItem(oBody, exu.ComputeItemType.PositionJacobian, localPosition=[0.1,0,0])
```



Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`computeItemTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/computeItemTest.py) (TM)


(sec-systemutilities-computesystemgraph)=
## Function: ComputeSystemGraph

[`ComputeSystemGraph(mbs, showLoads = True, showSensors = True, useItemNames = False, useItemTypes = False, addItemTypeNames = True, multiLine = False, addItemData = False, addAnnotations = False)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/systemUtilities.py#L470)

- **function description**: the graph of a MainSystem as networkx graph, without drawing: one graph node per item and the edges object - node, marker - object or node, connector - marker, load - marker, sensor - object or node; for an analysis of the structure, e.g. its connected parts or the items without connection; needs networkx
- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem
  - `showLoads`: if True, the loads are included
  - `showSensors`: if True, the sensors are included
  - `useItemNames`: if True, the graph nodes are named by the names of the items instead of their kind and number
  - `useItemTypes`: if True, the graph nodes are named by the item types (MassPoint, JointRevolute, ...) and number
  - `addItemTypeNames`: with useItemTypes, the kind (Node, Object, ...) is put in front
  - `multiLine`: if True, the names are split into lines, for drawing
  - `addItemData`: if True, each graph node gets the attributes 'type' (e.g. 'ObjectMassPoint'), 'ID' (the item number) and 'name'
  - `addAnnotations`: if True, each graph node gets the attribute 'annotations': the data of the item except graphics data, item numbers, names and types
- **output**: the networkx Graph; each graph node has the attributes 'basicType' (Node, Marker, Object, Load, Sensor) and 'color', each edge 'color'

*example*:

```python
  import networkx as nx
  G = ComputeSystemGraph(mbs)
  print('connected parts:', nx.number_connected_components(G))
```



Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`systemUtilitiesTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/systemUtilitiesTest.py) (TM)


(sec-systemutilities-drawsystemgraph)=
## Function: DrawSystemGraph

[`DrawSystemGraph(mbs, showLoads = True, showSensors = True, useItemNames = False, useItemTypes = False, addItemTypeNames = True, multiLine = True, fontSizeFactor = 1., layoutDistanceFactor = 3., layoutIterations = 100, showLegend = True, tightLayout = True, showGraph = True, addItemData = False, addAnnotations = False) -> list`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/systemUtilities.py#L606)

- **function description**: draw the graph of a MainSystem with matplotlib, from ComputeSystemGraph; several options adjust the appearance; the layout is random, so it differs from run to run; needs networkx and matplotlib
- **input**:
  - `mbs`: MainSystem to be operated with
  - `showLoads`: toggle appearance of loads in mbs
  - `showSensors`: toggle appearance of sensors in mbs
  - `useItemNames`: if True, object names are shown instead of basic object types (Node, Load, ...)
  - `useItemTypes`: if True, object type names (MassPoint, JointRevolute, ...) are shown instead of basic object types (Node, Load, ...); Note that Node, Object, is omitted at the beginning of itemName (as compared to the reference manual); item classes become clear from the legend
  - `addItemTypeNames`: if True, type nymes (Node, Load, etc.) are added
  - `multiLine`: if True, labels are multiline, improving readability; ignored if showGraph = False
  - `fontSizeFactor`: use this factor to scale fonts, allowing to fit larger graphs on the screen with values < 1
  - `layoutDistanceFactor`: this factor influences the arrangement of labels; larger distance values lead to circle-like results
  - `layoutIterations`: more iterations lead to better arrangement of the layout, but need more time for larger systems (use 1000-10000 to get good results)
  - `showLegend`: shows legend for different item types
  - `tightLayout`: if True, uses matplotlib plt.tight_layout() which may raise warning
  - `showGraph`: if True, graph is plotted with matplotlib
  - `addItemData`: if True, specific data is added to the graph nodes, to be used for deeper analysis of system graphs
  - `addAnnotations`: add data node graphs (not shown), except for graphics data, item numbers, names and types (which are already available in graph data or edges)
- **output**: (type: [Any, Any, Any]) returns [networkx, G, items] with nx being networkx, G the graph and item what is returned by nx.draw_networkx_labels(...)

- **NOTE**: this function is directly available in MainSystem (mbs); it should be directly called as mbs.DrawSystemGraph(...). For description of the interface, see the MainSystem Python extensions, {ref}`sec-mainsystemextensions-drawsystemgraph`


(sec-module-systemutilities-class-systemquantity)=
## CLASS SystemQuantity (in module systemUtilities)

**class description**: a quantity of the whole system with named components - an energy, a drift - from the contributions of its items; the base class of SystemEnergy and SystemConstraintDrift, which define the components and how an item contributes

- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem, assembled
  - `items`: None for all items that contribute, or a list of the items to take into account (ObjectIndex, NodeIndex, LoadIndex)
  - `skipUnavailable`: if True, an item that has the quantity but cannot compute it with its parameters (a user function) is left out and listed in .unavailable; if False, it raises
- **notes**: The contributing items are collected once, when the object is created: .items, and .unavailable, a list of (item, type name, component, reason); call Refresh() after the system changed. Compute() gives one value per component, in the order of .names; ComputeItems() the contribution of each item; AddSensor() adds a SensorUserFunction that records the components - call mbs.Assemble() after it.

  - `writeToFile`: write the values to a file

(sec-module-systemutilities-class-systemenergy(systemquantity))=
## CLASS SystemEnergy(SystemQuantity) (in module systemUtilities)

**class description**: the energies of the whole system (#2202): the output variables KineticEnergy and PotentialEnergy of its objects and the potential of its constant loads, LoadPotentialEnergy; components 'kinetic', 'potential' (of the objects), 'loads' and 'total', their sum

- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem, assembled
  - `items`: None for all objects and loads, or a list of the ObjectIndex and LoadIndex to take into account
  - `skipUnavailable`: if True, an object that has an energy but cannot compute it with its parameters (a user function) and a load without a potential are left out and listed in .unavailable; if False, they raise
- **notes**: The kinetic energy of a body computed from its mass matrix exists in the current configuration only.

*example*:

```python
  energy = SystemEnergy(mbs)
  [kinetic, potential, loads, total] = energy.Compute()
  sEnergy = energy.AddSensor()
  mbs.Assemble()
```

(sec-module-systemutilities-class-systemconstraintdrift(systemquantity))=
## CLASS SystemConstraintDrift(SystemQuantity) (in module systemUtilities)

**class description**: the drift of the constraints of the whole system (#565): components 'positionDrift', the largest absolute residual of the position-level constraints (ComputeItemType.ConstraintDrift), and 'velocityResidual', the largest absolute residual of the equations at velocity level (ComputeItemType.AlgebraicEquations_t); the items are the objects and nodes with algebraic equations, e.g. joints and Euler parameter nodes

- **input**:
  - `mbs`: the MainSystem, assembled
  - `items`: None for all constraints and nodes with algebraic equations, or a list of the ObjectIndex and NodeIndex to take into account
  - `skipUnavailable`: if True, an item without the velocity level (ObjectJointSliding, ObjectJointSliding2D) gives NaN for velocityResidual and is listed in .unavailable; if False, it raises
- **notes**: The residuals are those of the current state; the configuration of Compute and of the sensor must be the current one. The residual vectors themselves: mbs.ComputeConstraintResiduals() for the system, mbs.ComputeItem(item, ComputeItemType.ConstraintDrift) for one item. The drift check of the solver, timeIntegration.generalizedAlpha.checkConstraintDrift, uses the same definition of the drift.

*example*:

```python
  drift = SystemConstraintDrift(mbs)
  sDrift = drift.AddSensor()
  mbs.Assemble()
  mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings, solverType=exu.DynamicSolverType.TrapezoidalIndex2)
  print('largest drift', max(mbs.GetSensorStoredData(sDrift)[:,1]))
```
